resolved_conflicts.explanation: The list's entry carries the note 1808. Sherpa Guides dates the Martello lookout tower to 1812-1815 and gives 1808 as the year the federal government acquired jurisdiction over the area. The story follows Sherpa.
Explore Tybee says the government approved the fort in 1855; the Tybee Island blog says the U.S. established it in the late 1890s. The story reports both.

sources.title: Discovering Tybee Island's Rich Military History: Exploring Fort Screven, Tybee Post Theater and Fort Pulaski

notes_for_editor: The list's Fort Screven entry (GA317) is matched to the Martello lookout tower in the Sherpa history by name and place; no source names the list entry directly, so the identity is an inference. The list's 1808 note conflicts with Sherpa's 1812-1815 build date; the story follows Sherpa and says so. Sherpa is the only source for the tower's uses, the 1913 fire and the 1914 demolition, so check those dates against a primary source (Georgia Archives or a Tybee museum record) before relying on them. No source describes the site today beyond 'nothing is visible'. No photographs found. Research: one WebSearch (snippets only, not used as evidence) and four page reads.
